question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit target-agent profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported security boundary?
rationale: The requested fix adds public config and changes workspace file access for child sessions, which automation cannot choose safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Keep explicit profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where isolation requires configured child agent profiles and `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if needed.

options.title: Add narrow opt-in config
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` as a strict same-agent default-child override with schema, docs, doctor/security review, and focused workspace regression coverage.

options.title: Defer to broader workspace policy
options.body: Hold this until subagent workspace, task `cwd`, sandbox policy, and skill workdir isolation are designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where isolation requires configured child agent profiles and `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent security-boundary work on spawned workspace overrides makes this the closest available owner for deciding whether a new public workspace config is acceptable.
